extracted.intended_audience: IP statisticians, policy makers, WIPO staff, national/regional trademark offices, IP researchers and practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and definitions for compiling, presenting and interpreting global trademark statistics (application and registration class counts, resident/non-resident breakdowns, sector/class distributions, and procedural indicators) as used in WIPO's World Intellectual Property Indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent application class count
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed at some regional IP offices are equivalent to multiple applications in countries that are members of the organizations establishing those offices. For example, to calculate the number of equivalent applications for the EUIPO, each application is multiplied by the corresponding number of EU member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application filed with the EUIPO by an applicant residing outside the EU is counted as 28 applications abroad (equivalent to the 28 member countries of the EU in 2019). An application filed by an applicant residing in an EU country is counted as 1 resident application and 27 applications abroad for 2019. The same multiplier is applied to the classes specified in these applications. The equivalent application class count concept is used for reporting data by origin. Note: equivalent application class counts differ from absolute class counts, which do not take into account the multiplying effect of regional offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office data vs origin data (resident / non-resident)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark applications received by offices from resident and non-resident applicants are referred to as office data, whereas applications filed by applicants at a national/regional office (resident applications) or at foreign offices (applications abroad) are referred to as origin data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report provides statistics based on the origin (residence) of the applicant to complement office-based filing activity. Figures and maps use either office data or origin data depending on context (e.g., equivalent application class counts by origin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application class count (class counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class counts count the number of Nice classes specified in applications and are used to make application activity internationally comparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class counts allow meaningful international comparisons even where single-class and multi-class filing systems differ across offices. Class counts are used across many indicators (application class counts, registration class counts, equivalent counts). See glossary for formal definition of class count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident share / Non-resident share (%)
rubrics_metrics.description: The resident share is the percentage of application (or registration) activity originated by applicants residing in the office's country/region; the non-resident share is the complementary percentage coming from abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout to characterize whether filing activity at an office is domestic- or foreign-driven. Figures show resident and non-resident class counts and the non-resident share as a percent of totals (e.g., B3, B6, B10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment of application class counts by GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident trademark application class count can be adjusted relative to GDP to account for differences in economy size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report presents resident application class count per USD 100 billion GDP for selected origins (e.g., China, Republic of Korea, Brazil, Germany). Changes between 2009 and 2019 are used to highlight increases/decreases in class count per unit of GDP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment of application class counts by population
rubrics_metrics.description: Application class counts can be expressed per million population to reflect filing intensity relative to population size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data presented as resident application class count per million population for selected origins (e.g., China 5,425 per million in 2019). Useful to compare countries with different population sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Nice Classification and grouping into industry sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks are registered in relation to particular classes of goods or services using the Nice Classification; the 45 Nice classes are grouped into 10 industry sectors for reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nice class distributions and sectoral groupings provide insights into which goods/services attract filing activity abroad. The report identifies top classes (e.g., class 9) and top sectors (e.g., research & technology, health, clothing). Service-related classes share and trends (e.g., 11 service-related classes accounted for 30.4% of Nice classes in 2019) are highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madrid route vs Paris route (counting Madrid System activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can file directly at each national/regional office (Paris route) or file an international registration through the Madrid System (Madrid route). Madrid System filings are reported separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Madrid System allows a single application in one language with designations. The Madrid System covers many countries and its activity (international applications, designations, origins, top designated members) is reported (figures B47–B50). Madrid applications are estimated because of time lags in transmittal from offices of origin to the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations and registration class counts; comparability caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: After examination, an office may register a trademark; registrations and the classes specified in registrations are reported as registration class counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of registrations can fluctuate because of resource allocation to examination. Therefore, it is not possible to accurately compare the number of applications filed in a given year with the number of registrations issued by that office in the same year. The report nevertheless presents registration totals, growth rates, and registration class counts (e.g., B4, B5, B17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations in force / active trademarks and longevity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations in force are trademarks maintained (renewed) and reported as active registrations; metrics include totals in force, distribution by origin/office, average age and percentage remaining in force by registration year cohorts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademarks can be maintained indefinitely via renewals. The report estimates number of registrations in force (e.g., 58.2 million active registrations in 2019 across 146 offices) and reports cohort survivorship (e.g., 22.2% of trademarks registered in 1995 remained in force in 2019; over 65% for those registered in 2010 and later). Metrics include average age and share of registrations in force dating back to specific years (figures B37–B40).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and office performance indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural statistics describing office performance and workload are reported, including examination outcomes distribution, pending applications, number of examiners, duration of examination, third-party oppositions, and appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural indicators are presented for selected offices (figures/tables B41–B46) and are intended to contextualize registration activity and backlog dynamics (e.g., why registrations may fluctuate year-to-year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of regional office data to income groups for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Data for regional offices are allocated to income groups based on the income status of most member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: EUIPO data are allocated to the high-income group because most EU member states are high-income. For the same reason, data for ARIPO and OAPI are allocated to the low-income group. This affects aggregates by income group (figure B7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of WIPO estimates and office coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals and many aggregates are WIPO estimates using data covering a defined set of IP offices (168 offices referenced in the report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes indicate coverage and estimation methods (e.g., world totals are estimates using data covering 168 IP offices; Madrid applications are estimated due to transmittal lags). Users should consider coverage when interpreting global totals and growth rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident filing origin and flow indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics about the origins of non-resident filings at selected offices (flows of non-resident application class counts between top origins and offices) are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures show which foreign origins account for shares of non-resident filing at particular offices (e.g., U.S., China, Germany shares of non-resident filing in India, U.S., China, EUIPO). These flows contextualize international filing patterns (figure B25 and B24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of a standard set of figures and tables (B1–B53)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report defines a standard catalogue of figures and tables (B1–B53) covering trends, breakdowns by office and origin, Nice class/sector distributions, GDP/population adjustments, collective/certification applications, registrations in force, procedural data, Madrid System statistics, and statistical tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed figures/tables specify the metrics and breakdowns WIPO presents (e.g., B1 Trend in trademark applications worldwide; B7 application class counts by income group; B26 distribution by top Nice classes; B33 resident class count per USD 100 billion GDP; B41 distribution of examination outcomes; B47 trend in Madrid applications; B51–B53 detailed tables). This acts as a template for what indicators the WIPO trademark statistics compilation should include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of Nice classes into goods vs services and service share reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The report distinguishes goods classes and service classes and reports the share of service-related classes in total filing activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In 2019, 11 service-related classes accounted for 30.4% of all Nice classes specified in applications filed abroad (up from 26.6% in 2005). The service/goods split is reported for offices and origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification about single-class vs multi-class system effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Trend data based on numbers of applications filed do not adjust for differences between single-class and multi-class filing systems across IP offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure notes remark that trend comparisons by application counts may be affected by different filing systems; class counts are used to mitigate this issue, but users should be aware of limitations when interpreting application number trends (e.g., B9 note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimation note for Madrid applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the time lag in transmittal of applications from offices of origin to the International Bureau (IB) of WIPO, Madrid applications are estimated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Madrid application counts presented (e.g., ~64,400 international applications in 2019) are estimates; changes in origin-country filings (e.g., strong growth from U.S.) are discussed with explicit numeric contributions to totals and growth.
